label: Final copy step, saturating for L=3; for longer sequences only when the fed-back input is 3/l/r
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, never on original or delimiter steps, and never where in_first=1. 86% of activation mass is on the last output step (to_go=0) and about 11% on the second-to-last. For L=3, the last step (t=5, outputting orig(2)) fires on essentially every sequence and makes up all of the strongest activations (55% of the mass, top-quartile coverage 0.76). For L>3, firing on the last step is sparse and weak, and depends on the fed-back input token: 3, l, r (and to a lesser degree g, z, n) raise the rate a lot. L=5 rarely fires at all. The diffuse low-magnitude tail on the last two steps of longer sequences is not captured, so precision and recall are incomplete.
